caption_recommended:
I did not need the hurt to become smaller.

I needed it to stop becoming your whole face.

That took honesty. An apology that did not hurry me. And time.

Looking at you again was not forgetting what happened. It was remembering that what happened and who you are were not the same sentence.

This is for the hurts that can be repaired—not the ones that keep asking you to survive them.
caption_alt: The hurt stayed true. It just stopped being the only truth I could see.
alt_text: Illustrated carousel slide 1: Late-night dining room, medium-wide diagonal geography shot from Aachu's side of the table. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. Aachu sits in the lower-left at a table set for two, still and upright rather than collapsed or crying. One visibly cold, untouched second plate, a serving bowl with a settled surface, and a burned-low plain candle prove she waited. The single empty chair intended for Zuv dominates the center foreground and creates a physical barrier. Zuv has just entered through the background doorway, rain-damp and stopped mid-step when he sees the table; he is present but visually smaller than the empty chair. His phone and keys remain in his own hands for this arrival beat. Aachu looks at the empty chair, not at him. The visual must read without copy as: he promised to be here, he was not, and his absence has become the first thing she sees. Exactly two people; no restaurant, server, flowers, gifts, background people, portraits, readable clock numbers, random lettering, or melodramatic tears.

Illustrated carousel slide 2: Same late-night dining room seconds later, low table-level view from just behind Aachu's right shoulder. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. The empty chair back fills the middle plane and clearly occludes part of Zuv's torso without intersecting or merging with him, so Aachu sees him through the geometry of the chair that represented his absence. Zuv is now fully inside the room. His keys already rest on a small side ledge; with one anatomically attached right hand, he deliberately places his phone face-down beside them, away from the table, while his left hand hangs open and empty at his side. He then stays beyond the chair rather than approaching or explaining with gestures. Aachu's partial profile and shoulder remain in the near foreground, her eye-line fixed through the chair slats toward him. The cold plate and burned-low candle stay visible at opposite lower corners. Camera compression makes the chair feel larger than him while keeping clear depth separation. No reflection, extra person, bouquet, apology note, speech bubble, readable clock, or random text.

Illustrated carousel slide 3: Later that night, a wide single-person hallway shot with exactly Aachu and no live background figure. A short row of three small framed memories sits on a narrow console. Their interiors use only soft, non-figurative washes of the couple's recurring clothing colors, with no discernible faces or bodies. Two frames are already face-down, showing only plain backs. Aachu is in the act of turning the third and final frame face-down with her right hand; her left hand stays naturally at her side. She looks at the moving frame, not toward camera. The repeated downturned rectangles create a visible action trail: one bad moment is being allowed to darken earlier memories. The dining room and Zuv are absent from view, but the cooled blue night light matches slides 1-2. Keep the action restrained and temporary, not destructive or terminal: no packed bag, removed ring, broken glass, torn paper, thrown object, crying fit, extra figure, mirror, silhouette, or random lettering.

Illustrated carousel slide 4: Following morning, over-Aachu-shoulder view from the dining-room doorway. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. Aachu is a partial foreground shoulder and cheek, stopped at the threshold but not hidden. Zuv now sits in the once-empty dining chair at the table, fully visible rather than occluded by its back. The cold plate and burned-out candle remain untouched between them as factual evidence of the previous night; he has not cleared the scene, replaced it with gifts, or staged a grand apology. His phone and keys remain face-down on the distant side ledge. He sits with both feet grounded, hands open and separate on his own thighs, eyes raised to Aachu, waiting rather than reaching. Soft neutral morning window light removes the hard chair-shadow geometry from slide 2. No breakfast makeover, flowers, gift, written apology, kneeling, tears, touch, smile, background person, or live reflection.

Illustrated carousel slide 5: Tight table-height reaction frame in the same morning dining room. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. Aachu has brought one of the face-down hallway frames into the room. In the lower foreground, her anatomically attached right hand lifts that single frame upright on the table with its plain back angled toward the viewer, so no interior image, face, or extra figure is visible. Her left hand stays relaxed in her own lap. The focal action is her gaze: for the first time in the deck, Aachu looks directly past the now-upright frame at Zuv with a steady, unsmiling but open expression. Zuv sits opposite in clear three-quarter view, meets her eye-line, and keeps both hands still on his thighs. The chair back no longer interrupts either face. The cold plate edge remains visible as a factual trace, not the focal subject. No touch, smile, hug, tears, apology card, readable image, extra person, reflection, or random lettering.

Illustrated carousel slide 6: Matched wide release using the same dining-room camera axis as slide 1, now in clear morning light. Exactly Aachu and Zuv and exactly two dining chairs. Aachu remains seated in her original chair. Zuv remains seated in the same once-empty chair from slides 1 and 4, but he has pulled and rotated that chair around to the adjacent side of the table, moving its back out of their sightline and leaving no third chair. Their body distance is conversational and smaller than slide 4, without a celebratory embrace. The cold plate and burned-out candle remain at the far edge of the table, proving the hurt was not erased. One memory frame stands upright near Aachu with its plain back toward the viewer; the other two stay face-down on the distant hallway console, making the ending a beginning rather than a magical restoration. Aachu speaks or listens with one relaxed hand open on the tabletop; Zuv listens with both hands visible and separate, no touching yet. Their faces are calm and fully recognizable. The image must read without copy as: the event is still part of the room, but it is no longer the only thing between them. No third chair, cleaned table, fresh meal, flowers, gifts, hug, kiss, halo light, hearts, background figure, live reflection, or instant-happy ending.
